# Neural and Learning-based Extraction


## Overview
Neural and Learning-based Extraction methods generate explicit triangle meshes from implicit representations (such as Signed Distance Fields or occupancy fields) by integrating the extraction process into a differentiable computational graph [G]. Unlike static algorithms like Marching Cubes, these methods allow the mesh geometry to be optimized via gradient descent to fit target scalar values or visual objectives [G]. They set themselves apart from sibling methods by treating grid deformations and topological weights as learnable parameters, enabling the resolution of topological ambiguities and the production of high-fidelity surfaces directly from neural network outputs [977-mise-meshing-isosurfaces-by-extracting.md][3669-flexicubes.md].

## Shared principles
This family inherits the discretized domain traversal and surface determination mechanisms from [Isosurface extraction](30-isosurface-extraction.md).

## Subtopics

### [MISE (Meshing Isosurfaces by Extracting)](977-mise-meshing-isosurfaces-by-extracting.md)
MISE generates a 3D mesh from a trained Differentiable Volumetric Rendering (DVR) model by querying an implicit occupancy field using an adaptive resolution algorithm [977-mise-meshing-isosurfaces-by-extracting.md]. It sets itself apart from uniform grid-based extraction methods by iteratively refining the sampling grid only where the occupancy field is ambiguous, thereby achieving high-fidelity meshes with significantly fewer model evaluations than static high-resolution marching cubes [977-mise-meshing-isosurfaces-by-extracting.md]. It is chosen when the implicit function is expensive to evaluate and the surface geometry is sparse or complex.

### [FlexiCubes](3669-flexicubes.md)
FlexiCubes is a differentiable isosurface extraction method that converts a Signed Distance Field (SDF) defined on a voxel grid into a triangle mesh, specifically designed for gradient-based optimization of geometric, visual, or physical objectives [3669-flexicubes.md]. Unlike static extraction methods, it introduces learnable per-cube weights (beta, alpha, gamma) and vertex deformations to resolve topological ambiguities and improve mesh quality during training [3669-flexicubes.md]. It builds on [Neural and Learning-based Extraction](6371-neural-and-learning-based-extraction.md) by providing a fully differentiable pipeline where the mesh geometry itself becomes an optimization variable [3669-flexicubes.md]. It is chosen when optimizing a mesh to fit a target SDF or when training a neural network to output geometry directly.

### [Ground Truth Generation for Neural Marching Cubes](3820-ground-truth-generation-for-neural-marching-cubes.md)
This method generates multi-resolution ground truth data for training Neural Marching Cubes (NMC) by computing per-grid-cell labels (case IDs, vertex positions, and plane parameters) from high-resolution voxel and surface intersection data [3820-ground-truth-generation-for-neural-marching-cubes.md]. It solves the problem of creating accurate training targets for a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) that predicts Marching Cubes configurations, enabling the network to learn the mapping from input fields to mesh primitives [3820-ground-truth-generation-for-neural-marching-cubes.md]. It differs from gradient-based methods by explicitly using computed surface intersection points and their normals for least-squares fitting to determine plane parameters, rather than relying solely on voxel occupancy or field gradients [3820-ground-truth-generation-for-neural-marching-cubes.md]. It is chosen when training a CNN to replace the extraction step for inference speed.

### [NeRF Density Field Mesh Extraction](4104-nerf-density-field-mesh-extraction.md)
This method extracts a triangle mesh from a trained Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) by querying the learned density field $\sigma$ on a 3D grid and applying the marching cubes algorithm at a specific threshold [4104-nerf-density-field-mesh-extraction.md]. It solves the problem of converting a volumetric, implicit representation into an explicit, watertight geometric mesh suitable for standard rendering pipelines or downstream geometry processing [4104-nerf-density-field-mesh-extraction.md]. It differs from its siblings, MISE and FlexiCubes, by relying on a fixed-resolution regular grid and a static isosurface threshold rather than adaptive refinement or learned cube templates [977-mise-meshing-isosurfaces-by-extracting.md][3669-flexicubes.md]. It is chosen for standard NeRF-to-mesh conversion where differentiability is not required.

### [Differentiable Marching Cubes](9774-differentiable-marching-cubes.md)
Differentiable Marching Cubes (DiffMC) is a mesh extraction method that generates explicit, watertight manifold meshes from scalar fields (typically Signed Distance Fields) by optimizing learnable grid deformations and per-cube weights [9774-differentiable-marching-cubes.md]. It builds on [Neural and Learning-based Extraction](6371-neural-and-learning-based-extraction.md) by introducing a deformable grid and differentiable FlexiCubes operator, allowing the mesh geometry to be optimized via gradient descent to fit target scalar values [9774-differentiable-marching-cubes.md]. Unlike static extraction methods, DiffMC dynamically adjusts surface representation through gradient-based optimization, producing significantly smoother surfaces than tet-based alternatives like DMTet when extracting from density fields [9774-differentiable-marching-cubes.md]. It is chosen when high-quality SDF-to-mesh conversion is needed within a differentiable optimization loop.

## Background
The family originates from the need to bridge the gap between implicit neural representations (like NeRFs and SDFs) and explicit polygonal meshes for downstream applications [G]. Early work focused on static extraction from NeRF density fields [4104-nerf-density-field-mesh-extraction.md]. The introduction of differentiable extraction, such as MISE [977-mise-meshing-isosurfaces-by-extracting.md], allowed for adaptive sampling. Subsequent developments like FlexiCubes [3669-flexicubes.md] and Differentiable Marching Cubes [9774-differentiable-marching-cubes.md] enabled end-to-end training of geometry by making the extraction process differentiable with respect to grid parameters. Ground truth generation methods [3820-ground-truth-generation-for-neural-marching-cubes.md] were developed to train CNNs for fast inference, replacing the differentiable optimization step with a learned approximation.
